newsitem.title: USA: Physicist Hawking gets Pentium upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Physicist Hawking gets Pentium upgrade.

text.p: The synthesized voice of famed Cambridge University physicist Stephen Hawking is now powered by Intel Corp's famous Pentium processor, thanks to a team of Silicon Valley engineers.

Intel said it has recently outfitted Hawking with a custom computer system designed for the professor's wheelchair which is based on its recently-unveiled 133-megahertz Pentium microprocessor with MMX technology.

Intel engineers crafted the system and presented it to the author of "A Brief History of Time," after Intel executives discovered during a dinner with Hawking last May that he was using a 486-based system they consider outdated.

"The interface was pretty primitive," said Steve Nachtsheim, vice president of Intel's mobile products group, who spent about 90 minutes studying Hawking's older system and asking the professor questions at the dinner last year.

Nachtsheim said a team of more than a dozen engineers chipped in to help design the specialized computer and worked with Words+, the company that provides the voice synthesizer software, to enhance it for use with Microsoft's Windows 95.
